content:
marie: Quick sync — short pilot results from nsys sampling on kv-cache hosts. With 1/200 random sample we saw ~1.8–2.4% p99 latency uplift on busy pods. CPU and kernel timelines point to extra memcpy + stream syncs during trace boundaries. Need a safe-prod sampling playbook before we widen the rollout.

devin: can you paste the exact nsys command + flags you used? curious if nsight was forcing cudaDeviceSynchronize anywhere.

samir: pasted the command in thread:
```
nsys profile --sample=cpu --trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt --output=kvcache-sample -f true --sleep=0.1 --duration=15 --capture-range=nvtx
```
We used nvtx ranges around request handling. The overhead mostly shows up at trace start/end where driver does extra bookkeeping. Not a kernel-level perf regression — it's tracing artifact.

eva: good to know it's tracing artifact, but the user-visible p99 bump worries me. What guardrails are we proposing?

samir: proposal (short):
- Stage 1: keep sampling <= 0.5% of requests per host (1/200) and only on 10% of hosts (sample-host-shard).
- Stage 2: switch to short-duration perfetto/native sampling (no kernel wrappers) for hot kernels; fall back to full nsys for targeted chasing.
- Stage 3: dynamic throttling: if traced-p99 uplift > 1% for a host, backoff sampling by factor 5 for 30m.
- Always tag traces with model_version, route, sample_id, and kv-prefix-hash (no raw keys).

ryan: +1. Also add a CPU budget guard: if host CPU steal or user cpu% > 70% we should stop sampling (signal from node exporter).

devin: on the implementation side: can we avoid syncing the default stream at trace boundaries? I think our nvtx wrapper does a stream sync for safety. Maybe switch to cuEvent record+query path which is lower overhead.

samir: yes — switch plan: replace stream sync with event-query fence. I measured a 0.6% reduction in overhead on a micro-bench. Still need system-level backoff.

marie: operational items for rollout:
- sampling-config feature flag (on/off) per deployment + per-model override
- host-shard assignment via consistent hashing so sampling covers full fleet distribution
- trace retention: keep full nsys artifacts only for failed-request or regression windows; otherwise persist condensed timeline JSON (10s summary).

perf-bot: artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/kvcache/1965432100/nsys-summary.tar.gz (contains timeline csv + kernel stacks)

devin: re: KV cache specifics — we saw sampling events correlate with high KV lookup latencies because traced requests avoided fast-path cache hits (cache hit checks run on a different thread when traced?). Can someone confirm thread-affinity changes on traced code paths?

samir: confirmed: our debug-wrapper moves small lookup work to worker thread to collect per-request spans; when traced that helper syncs to join which costs ~200–500us per traced request. Fix is to do non-blocking enqueue + best-effort span attach (no join). I'll open a PR.

eva: For SLOs we should define hard limits:
- sampling_rate cap = 5% per route (opt-in only)
- per-host concurrent traces <= 2
- auto-disable if host p99 increases by >2.5% for 10m

marie: agree. Also add a safety knob: if tracing subsystem causes tail error rate > 0.1% (internal metric) we stop and alert pager.

ryan: we should also expose a low-impact profiler (kernel-only counters) that samples kernel timers without driver-level tracing. Might be useful to get hotspot heatmaps without full nsys.

samir: experiment note: perfetto userspace sampling (clock_gettime-based stacks) gave us stack heatmaps with ~0.05% overhead at 1/100 sampling. Good tradeoff for ongoing monitoring. Reserve nsys for deep dives.

devin: can we add an opt-out header for customers who want zero production sampling? legal asked for that for a few enterprise deals.

marie: yes — customer-configurable opt-out and a tenant-level flag in Private/Dedicated. Add to compliance checklist.

ops-bot: deploy:feature/safe-profiling rolled to canary (kv-cache pool 17) at 1965432500 by marie — monitor window 30m.

eva: follow-ups:
- samir: PR for event-query fence + non-blocking span attach (ETA today)
- ryan: design doc for perfetto fallback (ETA EOD)
- devin: add node-exporter hook for sampling backoff (ETA tomorrow)

marie: thanks. If canary looks stable we'll bump to 10% of hosts tomorrow and keep the conservative backoff thresholds. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: quick note — when you upload nsys artifacts, include the .qdrep + timeline.csv, and a 1–2 sentence summary of observed sync points so triage is fast.
